content:
Things are getting pretty messy between Khloé Kardashian and her ex-husband Lamar Odom.

On Thursday’s episode of “The Kardashians,” Kardashian shared her reaction to Odom’s Netflix documentary, “Untold: The Death & Life of Lamar Odom” seven months after it premiered.

In the documentary, the former NBA player says his marriage to Kardashian was to further his own fame, and admitted he found the Kardashian family’s lifestyle attractive and wanted to experience it for himself. He also downplays her role in his recovery from his near-fatal overdose in 2015.

“I’m already Lamar Odom,” Odom says in the documentary, according to USA Today. “And I’m just kind of like watching how she lived, and their lifestyle, and I’m like, ‘I know this is where I want to be, like, this is how I want to live.’”

Kardashian explained why she took issue with the “distasteful” comments he made about her. She also suggested that she regretted participating in the documentary as a favor after Odom apparently asked her to, which she said made his remarks all the more hurtful.

“I did watch the Lamar documentary. I’m not too thrilled about it,” she said in a confessional during the Nov. 12 episode. “Because I’m watching the documentary and I’m like, ‘Wait, I took time out of my life to sit here and do a favor for you. I’m not being paid. I’m doing this because I’m trying to be nice.’”

Kardashian added, “There’s so many things that I just found really distasteful.”

The reality TV star declared that “the bridge is burned and there’s no more rope left to throw over” when it comes to her ties to Odom. “So he is dead to me,” she said.

Kardashian also took issue with her ex-husband’s “weird” reflection on their marriage in the documentary.

“You’re saying that you weren’t really in love with me, you married me just so you could be more popular in pop culture, all these things, which is so weird. Even if that is your truth, why don’t you say it without me being on the other side of these interviews?”

Elsewhere in “The Kardashians”episode, Scott Disick remarked that at one point Kardashian was “spoon-feeding [Odom] back to life,” to which Kardashian replied that she wasn’t seeking credit for caring for Odom.

“I don’t need you to thank me. Just don’t talk about me. Don’t discredit me,” she said.

While speaking about his documentary during an appearance on “Today” in April, Odom offered limited credit to Kardashian for nursing him back to health after his overdose. He stated that she helped save his life in “some ways,” but noted that ultimately “God saved my life.”

“She took care of me,” he said at the time. “God took care of me the most. What I came back from was like a medical miracle.”

Odom suffered a near-fatal drug overdose in October 2015 at the Love Ranch brothel in Crystal, Nevada. The former couple had signed divorce papers in 2015 a few months before Odom’s hospitalization in Nevada, but Kardashian halted the divorce petition to help take care of him during his recovery.

They later finalized their divorce in 2016.

Odom also spoke about his marriage with Kardashian on “Today,” telling the TV show he doesn’t “regret” marrying her and that “there was definitely a lot of love there.”

Odom and Kardashian met in August 2009 and wed one month later.

HuffPost has reached out to Odom’s reps for comment.
